terms.gloss: a partner in a company: a shareholder
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.3.50: sociī putandī sunt, quōs inter rēs commūnicāta est
terms.comment: In business Latin a partner; the sociī of the companies that farmed the public revenues (the pūblicānī) held shares (partēs) in them, the nearest Roman thing to a joint-stock company. See member.

evidence: Cic. Rab. Post. 4: magnās partēs habuit pūblicōrum (Lewis & Short, s.v. pars)
terms.comment: Pars is a share; Cicero says of Rabirius’ father that he held large shares in the public contracts. A modern share is āctia, āctiae f. (Traupman 377).

phrases.latin: Huic sociētātī multī sunt sociī; frāter meus parvam partem habet.
phrases.english: This company has many shareholders; my brother holds a small share.

sources: Lewis & Short: socius · Lewis & Short: pars
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 377, checked against the searchable text of the book.
